say.en: On result day, a results website crashes because lakhs of students open it at once. Now imagine attackers doing that on purpose, with thousands of hijacked computers. That is a DDoS attack. In this lesson: Tell ethical hackers from crackers.
Explain DoS and DDoS attacks.
Tell snooping from eavesdropping.

body.en: A hacker is a person with deep knowledge of computers and networks who finds weaknesses in them. Ethical (white-hat) *hackers* do this with the owner’s permission to find and fix security holes before criminals do. Crackers, or black-hat hackers, break into systems illegally to steal data, cause damage or demand money. Grey-hat hackers find weaknesses without permission but without malicious intent, which is still not legal. Weak passwords are one of the easiest ways in for a cracker.

points.en: White hat: with permission, to fix weaknesses
Grey hat: no permission, no malice: still not legal

title.en: On the board: DoS and DDoS

say.en: In a DoS attack, one attacker floods a server with requests.
In a DDoS attack, the attacker controls many infected computers called zombies, a botnet.
All the zombies hit the target server at once. Genuine users cannot get through.
Snooping secretly captures and analyses network traffic; eavesdropping listens in on a private conversation in real time.

narration.en: We draw a single attacker, then a botnet, and see why a distributed attack is so hard to stop.

say.en: Hackers and network attacks Match each term with what it describes.

body.en: A Denial of Service (DoS) attack floods a server or *network* with so many requests that its resources run out and genuine users are denied service. In a Distributed DoS (DDoS) attack the flood comes from many compromised computers, called zombies, that form a botnet under the attacker’s control; it is hard to block because the traffic comes from everywhere. Snooping is the secret capture and analysis of network traffic, for example with packet-sniffing tools. Eavesdropping is unauthorised real-time interception of a private communication such as a phone call, video conference or chat. Encryption is the main protection against both.

points.en: DoS: one source exhausts the server
DDoS: a botnet of zombies attacks together

problem.en: Identify the threat: (a) A college admission portal stops responding because 20,000 infected home computers send it requests at once. (b) An attacker on the same café Wi-Fi records all unencrypted traffic and studies it later. (c) A security firm is hired by a bank to break into its own website and report weaknesses. (d) Someone secretly listens to a video interview as it happens.

steps.en: (a) Many compromised computers flooding one server → DDoS
(c) With permission, to fix weaknesses → ethical (white-hat) hacking
(d) Real-time interception of a private conversation → eavesdropping

narration.en: Ask: is it many sources or one, live or recorded, with permission or without?

b Capturing and analysing traffic gives snooping.
c With permission, to fix weaknesses gives ethical (white-hat) hacking.

say.kn: ಉದ್ದದ ಪಾಸ್‌ವರ್ಡ್ ಮತ್ತು ಗೂಢಲಿಪೀಕರಣ ಬಲವಾದ ರಕ್ಷಣೆ.
